origins.section: On Java 21, Blocking Inside synchronized Holds the Carrier
A Virtual Thread Is Always a Daemon, at Normal Priority
On Java 21, Blocking Inside synchronized Holds the Carrier

recorded.pass:q-reload-under-monitor: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-reload-under-monitor: The page decides it: "On Java 21 a virtual thread can't unmount while it holds a monitor, or while it waits to enter one. It is **pinned**: its carrier blocks with it. The first request holds the monitor and sleeps on its carrier; the other three wait to enter on theirs. All four carriers are taken, so nothing else on the JVM runs until the refresh returns". It also says "The scheduler adds no carrier for this kind of pinning, so the unrelated task waited until the refresh returned." With 8 carriers, the holder and 7 waiters fill every carrier. The 1-second arrival falls inside the 3-second reload, so the health check waits until reload() returns. The page shows this with 4 carriers; 8 is the same mechanism scaled up. The 'says' is supported.
recorded.prompt:q-exporter-non-daemon: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-exporter-non-daemon: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-exporter-non-daemon: The page shows the throw: "setDaemon(false): java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: 'false' not legal for virtual threads". It also says "only a setter called on a thread you were handed fails, at run time", and the table gives "`setDaemon(false)` throws `IllegalArgumentException`". In the page's own code the exception is caught. The page never states in words that an uncaught exception stops main before start(); that step is ordinary Java exception semantics applied to the stem, which has no try/catch. The 'says' matches the page's output exactly.
recorded.prompt:q-trace-pinned: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-trace-pinned: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-trace-pinned: The page decides it: "To find the blocking ones, run with `-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=short`. It prints the stack where a pinned virtual thread blocked", followed by the sample "VirtualThread[#28]/runnable@ForkJoinPool-1-worker-1 reason:MONITOR / SyncTokens.token(Pinning.java:42) <== monitors:1" and then "It names the holder only; the three threads waiting to enter don't appear." So the property prints one stack: the holder's, inside refresh(). The 'says' is supported, including Java 21 and reason:MONITOR.
